questions.text: What is the primary reason for incorporating Design for Testability (DFT) features into a VLSI chip design?
options: A. To automatically correct software bugs when the operating system boots.
B. To improve the controllability and observability of internal nodes, making it easier to detect manufacturing defects.
C. To reduce the physical layout area and packaging costs of the silicon die.
D. To increase the maximum operating frequency of the functional logic.

questions.text: Which fault model assumes that a physical manufacturing defect causes a logic gate's input or output to remain permanently tied to a logic low state?
options: A. Stuck-At-1 (SA1)
B. Bridging Fault
C. Transition Delay Fault
D. Stuck-At-0 (SA0)

questions.text: In a standard MUX-based scan flip-flop, what signal directly determines whether the cell operates in its normal functional mode or its test shift mode?
options: A. Scan Data Out (SO)
B. Global Reset
C. Scan Enable (SE)
D. Scan Data In (SI)

questions.text: During the 'Shift' phase of scan testing, how are the test patterns loaded into a design's internal flip-flops?
options: A. In parallel, directly from all functional input pins simultaneously.
B. By executing a built-in firmware routine stored in the chip's ROM block.
C. Serially, where data moves through the chained flip-flops bit-by-bit on each active clock edge.
D. Via a dedicated wireless diagnostic interface built into the packaging.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of the 'Capture' phase in a standard scan test cycle?
options: A. To clear all internal registers back to an unknown 'X' state.
B. To stream the next test vector out to the external Automatic Test Equipment (ATE).
C. To allow the combinational logic's response to the loaded stimulus to be latched into the destination flip-flops.
D. To measure the total static power dissipation of the clock tree network.

questions.text: Which of the following lines represents a mandatory interface pin required by the standard IEEE 1149.1 Boundary Scan (JTAG) architecture?
options: A. CLK_OUT
B. BIST_ON
C. SE (Scan Enable)
D. TMS (Test Mode Select)

questions.text: How many stable states can the IEEE 1149.1 TAP Controller state machine stay in when the TMS signal is held constantly at a logic '1'?
options: A. It will eventually land and remain locked in the 'Test-Logic-Reset' state.
B. It will cause an electrical short circuit inside the instruction register.
C. It will navigate continuously through all 16 states in a loop.
D. It will freeze immediately in the 'Shift-DR' state.

questions.text: In a Full-Scan design, if a circuit contains 3 scan chains and the longest chain contains 150 flip-flops, how many clock cycles are needed to fully shift in a single test vector?
options: A. 50 cycles
B. 3 cycles
C. 150 cycles
D. 450 cycles

questions.text: What type of circuits are standard memory testing frameworks like Memory BIST (MBIST) specifically optimized to evaluate?
options: A. Analog-to-Digital converters exclusively
B. Asynchronous combinational decoder trees
C. External PCB signal trace connections
D. Embedded arrays like SRAMs, DRAMs, and ROMs

questions.text: Which software tool uses algebraic and structural algorithms to automatically generate digital test patterns for manufacturing defect screens?
options: A. LEF (Library Exchange Format) Parser
B. ATPG (Automated Test Pattern Generation)
C. P&R (Place and Route) Engine
D. STA (Static Timing Analysis)

questions.text: What is the function of the 'BYPASS' instruction in the IEEE 1149.1 boundary scan standard?
options: A. It completely disconnects power from the IC to protect it from overcurrent.
B. It routes test data through a single-bit register to shorten the scan path to other chips on the board.
C. It duplicates the scan chains to run twice as fast.
D. It forces all core combinational logic nodes to an inverse state.

questions.text: Which defect scenario is a basic 'Transition Delay Fault' model intended to capture?
options: A. An incorrect logic gate optimization performed by the synthesis engine.
B. A net that switches its logic state successfully, but takes longer than the allowed clock period to complete the transition.
C. A leakage current spike in the substrate during static conditions.
D. A permanent short circuit between a signal line and the VDD rail.

questions.text: What design rule constraint must be met to ensure a flip-flop can be safely included in a standard scan chain?
options: A. It must be constructed using exclusively low-threshold voltage transistors.
B. Its output must connect directly to an external chip pin without driving other internal gates.
C. Its clock pin must be directly controllable from an external test clock source during the shift phase.
D. It must bypass all connected combinational logic networks entirely during functional mode.

questions.text: What is the role of a 'Compactor' block in an advanced scan compression architecture?
options: A. To check for setup and hold timing violations inside the clock tree.
B. To combine the outputs of many internal scan chains into a few external channels for the ATE to read.
C. To store failing memory bit cell coordinates inside an internal volatile array.
D. To step down high incoming supply voltages to safe levels.

questions.text: Which JTAG instruction is used to apply test patterns to external board-level interconnects between different integrated circuits?
options: A. BYPASS
B. EXTEST
C. SAMPLE
D. INTEST

questions.text: What does an ATPG tool do during its 'Fault Simulation' routine?
options: A. It measures the physical thickness of the chip's oxide layer.
B. It repairs broken physical connections within the logic gates.
C. It evaluates how many targeted faults are detected by a given set of test patterns.
D. It shifts data into the MBIST controller via the serial JTAG interface.

questions.text: What structural issue can arise if two scan flip-flops in the same chain are placed far apart, and the clock signal arrives at the second flip-flop significantly later than the first?
options: A. Setup time violation during functional mode
B. Hold time violation during the scan shift phase
C. The chip permanently enters a low-power sleep state.
D. The MBIST address generator stops sequencing.

questions.text: Why are standard 'March Tests' used instead of random data patterns to verify embedded memory structures?
options: A. They use structured, linear combinations of reads and writes designed to isolate memory-specific defects like coupling or address decoder faults efficiently.
B. They are designed to verify analog operational amplifiers exclusively.
C. They reduce the total silicon area overhead of the memory wrapper to zero.
D. March tests run without requiring a clock signal.

questions.text: In DFT terminology, what does 'Test Overhead' refer to?
options: A. The additional silicon area, pins, and timing delays introduced by adding test structures into a design.
B. The time spent by field engineers manually debugging system software errors.
C. The maximum voltage limit supported by the chip's IO pads.
D. The cost of renting the physical building where the production testers operate.

questions.text: Which of the following metrics is computed by dividing the number of manufacturing faults detected by a test program by the total number of testable faults defined in the design netlist?
options: A. Fault Coverage
B. Clock Skew Margin
C. Yield Loss Parameter
D. Power Efficiency Ratio
